title: Tensor products of fields with one finitely generated extension are Noetherian Cohen–Macaulay
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $K/k$ and $L/k$ be field extensions [def-pc-field-extension]. Assume at least one extension is finitely generated as a field: for example, $K=k(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ for finitely many elements $a_i\in K$, meaning the smallest subfield containing $k$ and these elements is $K$ (or the analogous condition for $L$). Form the commutative ring $T=K\otimes_kL$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with multiplication $(a\otimes b)(c\otimes d)=ac\otimes bd$. Then $T$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and Cohen–Macaulay: for every prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset T$, its localization $T_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a Noetherian local ring and satisfies $\operatorname{depth}(T_{\mathfrak q})=\dim T_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-depth; def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. No algebraicity, separability, or perfectness is assumed.

source.place: Tag 045M (lemma-tensor-fields-CM), statement; Cohen–Macaulay ring is spelled out by its local definition.

proof.text: The swap $K\otimes_kL\longrightarrow L\otimes_kK$, $u\otimes v\mapsto v\otimes u$, is a ring isomorphism with its swap as inverse, by bilinearity and the multiplication in the statement. Thus assume $K=k(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finitely-generated-field-finite-transcendence-basis] to choose algebraically independent $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in K$ with $K$ algebraic over $F=k(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$. Since $F\subset K$ and $k\subset F$, the original generators also give $K=F(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$. They are algebraic over $F$, so [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-generators-finite-extension] makes $K$ a finite-dimensional $F$-vector space. Choose a finite $F$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ of $K$. No assertion of separability is used.

source.place: Tag 045M, lemma-tensor-fields-CM, proof: choose a finite extension of a purely transcendental extension; Fields Tags 030F (lemma-transcendence-degree) and 09GH (lemma-algebraic-finitely-generated).

proof.text:
Put $B=k[t_1,\ldots,t_r]\subset K$, $W=B\setminus\{0\}$, and $P=L[t_1,\ldots,t_r]$. Algebraic independence identifies $B$ with the polynomial ring on these symbols, and $F=W^{-1}B$: the fractions in $B$ form exactly the smallest subfield containing $k$ and all $t_i$. There is a ring isomorphism $B\otimes_kL\cong P$ sending $t^\alpha\otimes l$ to $lt^\alpha$; its inverse sends $\sum_\alpha l_\alpha t^\alpha$ to $\sum_\alpha t^\alpha\otimes l_\alpha$. The two maps preserve multiplication by the monomial rule and are inverse by bilinearity. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] with base $k$, algebra and module $B$, multiplicative set $W$, and module $L$. It identifies
$$A:=F\otimes_kL\cong W^{-1}(B\otimes_kL)\cong W^{-1}P.$$
The localization formula $(b\otimes l)/w\mapsto (b/w)\otimes l$ respects products, since both products multiply the two numerators and the two denominators. Here $W$ in $P$ denotes its image under the coefficient inclusion; no nonzero polynomial in $B$ becomes zero in $P$.

source.place: Tag 045M, lemma-tensor-fields-CM, proof: the purely transcendental tensor factor is a localization of a polynomial ring; Tag 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization), with tensor associativity Tag 00D2.

proof.text: The field $L$ is Noetherian because its only ideals are $(0)$ and $L$, and its only prime is $(0)$, with localization $L_{(0)}=L$. Its Krull dimension is zero. Its maximal ideal is zero, so its depth is zero: the empty regular sequence exists and a positive-length sequence in that ideal begins with zero, whose multiplication on the nonzero module $L$ is not injective. Therefore $L$ satisfies every hypothesis of [lem-trf-polynomial-algebra-cm]. Applying that node with coefficient ring $L$ and $r$ variables shows that $P$ is Noetherian and that every $P_{\mathfrak r}$ has depth equal to dimension. Since $A=W^{-1}P$, [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] also shows that $A$ is Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 045M, lemma-tensor-fields-CM, last sentence, using Tag 00ND (lemma-CM-polynomial-algebra) and Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence).

proof.text:
Fix a prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A=W^{-1}P$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-quotient-by-prime], its contraction $\mathfrak r\subset P$ is prime, avoids $W$, and $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak r A$. The fraction formulas give mutually inverse local ring maps
$$P_{\mathfrak r}\longrightarrow A_{\mathfrak p},\quad f/g\longmapsto(f/1)/(g/1),\qquad
 A_{\mathfrak p}\longrightarrow P_{\mathfrak r},\quad (a/s)/(b/t)\longmapsto at/(sb).$$
In the second formula $s,t\in W$, and $b/t\notin\mathfrak p$ means $b\notin\mathfrak r$; hence $sb\notin\mathfrak r$. The fraction equality relation makes the maps well-defined, and multiplication and cancellation show their composites fix every fraction. Thus $A_{\mathfrak p}$ has the same depth and dimension as $P_{\mathfrak r}$, so is Cohen–Macaulay by step 3. The local-ring assertion is part of [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and its Noetherianity follows from [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian].

source.place: Tag 045M, lemma-tensor-fields-CM, localization sentence; Tag 00E3 (lemma-spec-localization) and the fraction construction in Tag 00CO (definition-localization).

proof.text:
The $A$-algebra $T=K\otimes_kL$ is identified with $A\otimes_FK$ by
$$ (f\otimes l)\otimes u\longmapsto fu\otimes l,\qquad
 u\otimes l\longmapsto(1\otimes l)\otimes u.$$
These formulas are balanced over $k$ and $F$, preserve multiplication, and are mutually inverse on the displayed generators. If $\lambda_i:K\to F$ are the coordinate maps in the basis $(e_i)$ of step 1, the maps
$$A^d\longrightarrow A\otimes_FK,\quad(c_i)\longmapsto\sum_i c_i\otimes e_i,\qquad
 A\otimes_FK\longrightarrow A^d,\quad c\otimes u\longmapsto(c\lambda_i(u))_i$$
are inverse $A$-linear maps: $\lambda_i(e_j)=\delta_{ij}$ checks one composite, and $u=\sum_i\lambda_i(u)e_i$ checks the other. Consequently $T$ is a finite free $A$-module. This construction works for inseparable finite extensions as well.

source.place: Tag 045M, lemma-tensor-fields-CM, proof: the displayed ring map is finite free; the coordinate verification uses the universal property in Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product).

proof.text: By step 3, $A$ is Noetherian, and step 5 exhibits finitely many $A$-module generators of $T$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian] makes $T$ Noetherian. By [lem-sc-affine-standard-cover-finite-free-local-fp-flat], its finite free $A$-module structure makes $A\to T$ flat. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], the same finiteness makes $A\to T$ integral. These are statements about the global finite free map, before localization at a prime of $T$.

source.place: Tag 045M, lemma-tensor-fields-CM, Noetherian and finite-free assertions; Tags 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), 00NX (lemma-finite-projective), 00GK (lemma-finite-is-integral).

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak q\subset T$ be any prime and $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap A$. Put $R=A_{\mathfrak p}$ and $S=T_{\mathfrak q}$. They are local rings with the displayed prime-generated maximal ideals by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and they are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] and steps 3 and 6. The map $R\to S$ exists since elements of $A\setminus\mathfrak p$ map outside $\mathfrak q$, hence become units; it is local since $\mathfrak pR$ maps into $\mathfrak qS$. Apply [lem-pc-affine-flat-module-local-criterion] to the flat $A$-module $T$ to conclude that $S$ is flat over $R$. Step 4 gives $\operatorname{depth}R=\dim R$.

source.place: Tag 045M, lemma-tensor-fields-CM, application of Tag 00R5 (lemma-finite-flat-over-regular-CM), localized using Tag 00HT (lemma-flat-localization), part (6).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime], $\dim S$ is the supremum of the lengths of strict prime chains in $T$ lying below $\mathfrak q$. For any such chain $\mathfrak q_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak q_m\subseteq\mathfrak q$, integrality of $A\to T$ from step 6 and [lem-weil-pbc-integral-incomparability] show that its contractions are a strict prime chain in $A$ lying below $\mathfrak p$. The same dimension-chain node applied to $A,\mathfrak p$ bounds its length by $\dim R$. Taking suprema yields $\dim S\leq\dim R$. This uses incomparability for $A\to T$ itself; it makes no finiteness or integrality claim about $R\to S$.

source.place: Tag 045M, lemma-tensor-fields-CM, finite-flat Cohen–Macaulay step; the dimension-bound hypothesis of Tag 00R5 (lemma-finite-flat-over-regular-CM), using Tag 00GT (lemma-integral-no-inclusion) and Tag 00E3 (lemma-spec-localization).

proof.text:
The map $R\to S$ is flat and local between Noetherian local rings by step 7, so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-depth-formula] gives
$$\operatorname{depth}S=\operatorname{depth}R+\operatorname{depth}(S/\mathfrak pRS)\geq\operatorname{depth}R=\dim R.$$
The inequality uses only nonnegativity of depth in [def-weil-pbc-depth]. The ring $S$ is nonzero: $A$ is a nonzero localization of the nonzero polynomial ring $P$, and step 5 makes $T$ finite free of positive rank over $A$, so its prime localization $S$ is nonzero. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-depth-le-support-dimension] to the nonzero finite $S$-module $S$ itself: its support is all of $\operatorname{Spec}S$, because each prime localization has a proper maximal ideal and is nonzero. Thus $\operatorname{depth}S\leq\dim S$. Together with step 8,
$$\dim R\leq\operatorname{depth}S\leq\dim S\leq\dim R.$$
In particular $\operatorname{depth}T_{\mathfrak q}=\dim T_{\mathfrak q}$ for every $\mathfrak q$. This proves the required Cohen–Macaulay assertion, and step 6 already proved Noetherianity. The swap of step 1 handles the case where only $L/k$ is finitely generated.

source.place: Tag 045M, lemma-tensor-fields-CM, application of Tag 00R5 (lemma-finite-flat-over-regular-CM), with its depth inequality supplied by Tag 0337 (lemma-apply-grothendieck); upper bound Tag 00LK (lemma-bound-depth).

The statement is unchanged and matches 045M: either extension may be of finite type, and Cohen-Macaulay is spelled out as Noetherian with depth = dim at every prime localization. The delivery has no new nodes. proof_deps equals the union of the steps' uses, there is no cycle, and there is no SGA citation. Every cited statement says what its step takes from it. Steps 1-2: finite transcendence basis, K finite over F = k(t), and F⊗L = W^{-1}L[t] via the localization-tensor node, with multiplicativity checked by hand. Step 3: L is a field (depth and dimension 0), so lem-trf-polynomial-algebra-cm and localization-Noetherian apply; r=0 is covered. Step 4: A_p is isomorphic to P_r by explicit fraction maps; the elementary marking is acceptable. Step 5: T is finite free over A = F⊗L via a basis of K over F, which also works for inseparable K. Step 6: T is Noetherian, flat and integral over A. Step 7: flatness localizes to R = A_p -> S = T_q, a local map. Step 8: dim S <= dim R by incomparability for the global integral map A -> T. Step 9: the flat local depth formula and depth <= dim Supp S = dim S give dim R <= depth S <= dim S <= dim R; the closed fibre S/pS is nonzero because the map is local. I tested k=K=L, K=k(t) with L=k(s), and an inseparable K = F_p(b)(b^{1/p}) with L = K, where T is Artinian with dimension and depth 0. The source has no error. No existing node states 045M or 00R5.
